# Breadth beyond words: primary-body screen, not novelty clearance

All linked arXiv versions below were downloaded in this lane on 30 October2026, hashed before PDF extraction and retained read-only; retrieval.jsonl records exact bytes, SHA256, URL, version and UTC. This is a set of separate primary research papers, not one survey's question list. Original attribution is distinguished from the nearest primary follow-up. Eight external exploratory families are rows1–8; row9 is a rejected family and is not an extra open lead. Together with the inherited word family these give ten family rows. They are NOT ten verified original-source/current-prior-cleared open questions. Several original attribution bodies and current registry comparison are missing. No rank implies eligibility.

1. **Strong blocking sets / minimal codes.** Bishnoi–Kakatelis, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.33219v1,23Oct2026, Section6 pp16–17: construct smaller explicit strong blocking sets in PG(k−1,q) without requiring the stronger line-avoidance property; codimension-two/hypergraph extensions are merged here. Definition: every hyperplane meets the set in a spanning set. Earlier Alon–Bishnoi–Das–Neri construction is attributed, not original-body cleared. Nearest actual body here Section3's field-sensitive partition parameter and Section4 line construction, not an unsolved existence assertion: O(qk) explicit existence is already public. Mechanism: replace line avoidance by direct hyperplane rank certification. Decisive calculation: identify an actual graph/code instance that fails avoidance while retaining all hyperplane ranks, then prove an asymptotic advantage. Objection: optimizing a known constant or a parameter instance is not eligible substantive resolution. **Low exploratory priority**, no quantified new bound invented.

2. **Minor-deletion kernelization beyond planar obstructions.** Ghazy–Greilhuber–Hartmann, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.18719v1,13Oct2026, introduction p3 and Theorems1.1/1.2: does F-Minor Deletion parameterized by solution size admit a polynomial kernel for every fixed finite F, beyond families containing a planar graph? This broad question is stated as major open, not a newly created conjecture. Actual Theorem1.1 gives distance-to-class compression lower bounds from unbounded minimal F-blocking sets, under disjoint-copy closure and connected F; Theorem1.2 shows bounded ordinary blocking sets do not characterize all lower bounds. End-of-paper Lemma6.15/Cor6.1 proof uses tidy leaf blocks/pathwidth constructions. Mechanism: extended blocking-set gadgets, not ordinary ones. Decisive step would require a new structural parameter that handles nonplanar obstructions. Objection: this is a major complexity problem, unsuitable for an elementary finite certificate attack. **Defer hard**. Do not mistake a lower bound in a different parameter for a solution-size answer.

3. **Asymptotic binary covering density / saturating sets.** Davydov–Marcugini–Pambianco–Wu, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.16078v2,11Oct2026, p4 quotes Green's Problem40: for fixed R let f(R) be the least asymptotic density constant for infinite sequences of binary linear covering codes of radius R; must f(R) tend to infinity as R tends to infinity? Its translation ell_2(r,R)=s_2(r−1,R−1) is Eq1.3. Green's original problem body is NOT fetched; attribution remains secondary in this primary construction paper. Theorems2.1 and5.4 and actual QM1 proof give improved fixed-R upper bounds, not the R→infinity answer. Mechanism: concatenation and parity-check partitions. Decisive calculation: obtain a bound uniform in R with the correct direction, rather than another R=2,3 constant. Objection: small-radius optimizations do not bear on divergence. **Defer**, no fixed parameter credited.

4. **Cameron–Liebler generator classifications.** D'haeseleer–Mannaert–Storme, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2503.08260v1,11Mar2025, Section1 Conjecture1.1 attributes an eventual classification to [21,Conj5.1], involving unions of point pencils, generators in nondegenerate hyperplanes, and versions excluding a fixed point. The printed n(q,k) quantification is insufficiently explicit here to promote a literal all-rank endpoint; original [21] is unread. Nearest actual body Section3, Proposition3.1 proof identifies Klein-quadric degree-one sets with point/plane sets in PG(3,q) having x or x+q incidence counts. This is a concrete finite algebraic classification setting; it does not prove the eventual all-polar-space conjecture. Mechanism: integral incidence eigenspaces plus Boolean constraints. Decisive calculation: read [21]'s actual quantified conjecture, then eliminate one proposed nontrivial parameter uniformly. Objection: spectral membership alone does not classify Boolean vectors. **Original-scope HOLD**, not ranked.

5. **Group-labeled matroid bases.** Liu–Oki–Xu, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.32798v1,23Oct2026, Theorem1 ALREADY proves weighted proximity for one abelian-group labeling: every min-cost base lies within |F| exchanges of a min-cost F-avoiding base, when one exists. Do not rediscover that statement or its FPT consequence. The paper's Conjecture3, attributed to Schrijver–Seymour1990, remains the broader base-label cardinality inequality with stabilizer H: |ell(M)| >= |H| min(sum_(Q in G/H) r(E(Q))−r(E)+1,|G|/|H|). Its printed theorem2 is prime-cyclic; theorem4 adds a unique min-cost label-base condition. Multiple-label proximity is merged here. Original1990 body unread. Mechanism: Kemperman–Scherk plus exchange; decisive step remove the unique-label hypothesis without assuming the conjectured stabilizer inequality. Objection: the newly published proximity theorem explicitly bypasses, rather than proves, that old conjecture. **Defer hard**; closest theorem is a public resolution of the easier lead.

6. **Pattern-avoiding permutahedra root location.** https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.06096v2,29Oct2026 updated version (first5Sep2026), Theorems3/4 give real negative zeros of H_d=h* of conv of (132,213)-avoiding permutations for d<=1000 and d>=2^62. The untouched intermediate interval is not claimed solved. This is one all-d family, not separate dimensions/outcomes; Davis–Sagan's earlier general pattern-set question is an attribution, original body unread. Actual Lemma6 proof pairs cut constraints with path-Laplacian constraints to establish the cube model; Sections5–9 use compatible refined Eulerian polynomials and weighted tail coordinates. The naive nonnegative-coordinate argument fails at a_(7,1)=−1/15 in the paper itself. Decisive calculation: sharpen the uniform weighted-tail estimates enough to join ranges, not perform the impossible intermediate enumeration. Objection: extending a finite range alone is a parameter instance; existing asymptotics may make this a technical constant improvement. **Provisional low-rank lead**, substantial/new classification not established.

7. **Inverse Kazhdan–Lusztig coefficient log-concavity.** Braden–Ferroni–Matherne–Nepal, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.01086v2,22Oct2026 (first1Oct2025), Conjecture1.2(c), attributed to Gao–Xie2021: for every matroid M the coefficients of inverse KL polynomial Q_M are log-concave. Merge the P/Z/Y variants conservatively. Their Conjecture1.3, the binomial-Hadamard real-rootedness strengthening of Xie–Zhang, is ALREADY REFUTED by this same version's rank19 example; never use its conjecture label as openness evidence. Actual deletion formula Theorem1.4 is the nearest mechanism: deletion, restriction and contraction terms have correction coefficients; log-concavity is not automatically preserved under such sums. Original GX21/XZ26 bodies unread. Decisive calculation: read the rank19 Q coefficients and check the weaker inequalities exactly before investing in a recurrence induction. Objection: a nonreal root of the binomial transform does NOT refute coefficient LC. **Provisional lead only**, no literal witness produced.

8. **Ehrhart Taylor threshold classification.** Liu–Zhang, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.03327v2,16Oct2026 (first3Sep2026), final paragraph p38: characterize natural classes with real Taylor threshold rho(P)=0, especially matroid base and smooth polytopes, and extremizers of tau(P)=floor((d−1)/2). Those are original author directions, not separate clauses counted as families. Actual Theorems1.5/1.7 ALREADY prove the universal INTEGER threshold floor((d−1)/2), including sharpness; do not nominate that bound. Formula1.4 expresses Taylor coefficients as L_P^(j)(k)/j!, equivalently weighted elementary-symmetric evaluations of the h* vector. Mechanism: exact signs in a structured h* family. Decisive step specify a genuinely unsolved natural class with an exact all-object endpoint; none selected here. Objection: an unspecified request to characterize natural classes is not an eligible theorem statement. **Defer vague endpoint**.

9. **Multiplicative Merino–Welsh.** Chen–Jin–Ma, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.27706v1,20Oct2026, actual Sections3–5: the all-matroid claim T(2,0)T(0,2)>=T(1,1)^2 is already false by Beke et al.2024; this paper proves all uniform q-thickenings with q>=3 satisfy it and the smallest doubled uniform counterexample has62 elements. Actual Lemma5.2 deletion–contraction proof shows every element of a minimal matroid counterexample lies in a two-element circuit or cocircuit, via the cross-term geometric-mean inequality. The graph version is a different surviving classical problem. **Reject the matroid target**; no graph theorem inferred. Not one of the eight exploratory open directions above; smallest-all-matroid enumeration is not promoted.

10. **Inherited quasiperiodic fixed-point converse.** Exact original/published bodies, hypotheses, two mechanisms, 92 positive lasso certificates, unresolved universal bridge and strongest objection: ATTACK.md. The only sustained attack; no full nomination.

Additional rejection controls, not extra families: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.40496v1 Theorems1.1/1.2 publicly solve crown/wheel/whirl real-rootedness; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.25863v2 already computes Birkhoff series through13 and World Cup through13, so those orders are unavailable; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.10513v2 publicly refutes IDP h*-unimodality and related stronger assertions. These downloaded bodies are negative screening evidence, not padding for new open targets.

# r232 — no full candidate; source and mechanism corrections

No discovery nomination. Root alone accepts/counts; context remains9 additional /39 total /next40. No Lean, manuscript, shared, git, public, browser or MathDB edits.

The actual published Levé–Richomme WORDS2013 chapter was obtained and read alongside frozen arXiv1304.6280v1. It retains the full fixed-point question and only the all-growing/nonperiodic Proposition7.1. Contrary to inherited notes, arXiv v1 contains the omitted Lemma6.5 proof in its Appendix; the published chapter omits it.

Two sustained mechanisms:

- Exact inverse-covering automaton/lasso route: a single nonrecurrent prefix is insufficient. Correct criterion excludes every shorter covering prefix as well. A failed196-positive output is preserved; corrected bounded search certifies92/196 maps (66 by either oriented unique-letter input). No universal inference.
- Growing-letter return-block route: the explicit delimiter code x→ab,y→abb maps NONquasiperiodic yxy^omega to abbab-covered abbab(abb)^omega. Delimiter synchronization alone cannot reflect nonquasiperiodicity. This obstructs a proposed bridge; it is not a source counterexample.

SCOUTING.md supplies eight new external exploratory directions, one rejected Merino–Welsh family and the inherited word family, with primary bodies from separate papers and exact missing-original limits. Additional solved papers serve only as rejection controls. This is NOT ten original/current-prior-cleared open targets. Compact history screen binds645 SUMMARY/discovery/SCOUTING files; no active wavelet/arithmetic target was adopted. Current complete proof-registry access remains HOLD under inherited denied routes, which were not retried.

ATTACK.md gives literal scope, closest actual proofs, corrected finite criterion, two gaps, decisive next calculation and strongest classical objection. FAILURES.md records bad diagnostics, failed helper execution and pre-freeze history/helper-read limits. PROOF.md intentionally absent: no full candidate. finalmanifest.json excludes itself and verification-receipt.json; verify.py runs separately under the mandatory guard.

# Discovery disposition: HOLD, no nomination

Exact endpoint and hypotheses: ATTACK.md paragraph1. Nearest original proof: arXiv1304.6280v1 Appendix p12, Lemma6.5; nearest published scope: WORDS2013 p191 Proposition7.1. Chronology: arXiv23Apr2013, proceedings2013, actual publisher and current arXiv API retrieval30Oct2026. No later complete solution located in this bounded screen; no priority clearance asserted.

The full arbitrary-morphism conclusion is unproved. Neither bounded letters nor periodic fixed points have been discarded. Needed bridge: fixed-point q-coverage must force an accepted lasso whose ORIGINAL input has no shorter covering prefix, or another witness/counterexample proving the entire endpoint. Both finite-state and return-block routes now have explicit stronger diagnostics/obstructions, but neither proves that implication.

Positive artifacts:92 exact binary lasso certificates, finite per-lasso nonquasiperiodicity criterion and delimiter-decoding obstruction. These are classical helpers/route obstructions, not credited discoveries, not a partial source theorem promoted as full. Strongest objection is classical finite-state subsumption plus unresolved universal quantification and current-prior gap.

Breadth conclusions and decisive calculations are in SCOUTING.md. Only provisional mechanism leads are retained; no candidate has substantive, originality, proof, independent review, formal or manuscript acceptance. Root alone determines count changes; this lane requests none.

# Eight additional family screens

These are eight distinct families beyond r230's eleven, not eight certified open problems. None is a discovery or novelty-cleared survivor. Actual question bodies were read in frozen primary authored problem collections, with primary PDF/text bindings regenerated locally. Old partial-result references below are attributed as the question author describes them; unless explicitly stated otherwise their original full proofs were NOT retrieved, and they cannot clear novelty or support acceptance. This limitation is a reason to defer, not a theorem-announcement substitute.

P = Anton Petrunin, *A gallery of open problems in geometry that keep me puzzled and amused*, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.11908v2, dated 7 September 2026, first version 13 October 2025. T = Yana Teplitskaya, *Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers*, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.18217v1, 22 November 2025. G = Szymon Głąb and Franciszek Prus-Wiśniowski, *Achievement sets – current results and open problems*, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.17285v1, 19 December 2025 (body dated 22 December). The recent collection dates do not make all their older questions recent; specific antecedents span 1995, 2003, 2005, 2020, and 2025. No familiar hard problem is ranked just for having an open label.

1. **Hilbert quotient versus biquotient.** P§3 pp3–4 asks whether every compact simply connected Riemannian manifold that is an isometric quotient of Hilbert space by isometries (or the target of a Riemannian submersion) is a compact Lie-group biquotient with bi-invariant metric. Actual nearby proof read: P sketches the EASY converse by rescaled products G^n and their Hilbert ultralimit, attributed to Lytchak; it also cites Terng–Thorbergsson 1995 §4 and Lebedeva–Petrunin–Zolotov 2019. Mechanism: recover a finite-dimensional Lie presentation from horizontal distributions. Decisive obstruction: the ultralimit construction only maps biquotients into the proposed larger class; it does not reconstruct group structure in reverse. **Reject for depth now:** no rigidity invariant, original 1995/2019 full proofs unread. This differs from r230's finite isotropy bound.

2. **Complete nested convex realization.** P§4 p4 asks which metrics on S^n are realizable as complete smooth convex hypersurfaces nested in complete smooth convex hypersurfaces in Euclidean space; it specifically raises whether nonnegative cosectional curvature suffices. The source explains necessity by a curvature-tensor calculation, and cites Petrunin 2003 for a local strictly positive version without completeness. Mechanism: globalize local convex realizations by controlled extension. Decisive check: an extension must preserve completeness at every nesting stage, not just embed each compact patch. **Defer:** exact 2003 proof unread, no global extension estimate. The Berger-sphere diagnostic suggested by the author is a tractable test but only a parameter instance, not the full classification. Distinct from nonsmooth two-convex planar sections.

3. **Length of an involution-fixed geodesic.** P§7 p6: if a closed geodesic γ is the fixed-point set of an isometric involution on (S³,g), sec(g)≥1, must length(γ)≤2π? Includes the analogous Alexandrov spherical-polyhedral question. The author gives a genuine nearby argument for S¹-actions: the quotient is a convex positively curved disc and the fixed geodesic becomes its boundary. Mechanism: replace the orbit-disc argument by a comparison invariant for the Z/2 quotient. Decisive check: involution quotients need not be discs, so boundary-length comparison cannot simply be imported. **Defer:** Fujioka 2025's nonsharp bound is cited but its proof unread; no involution replacement argument. No numerical length experiment is a universal proof.

4. **Faceting the Fubini–Study metric.** P§8 pp6–7: does CP² admit nonnegatively curved Euclidean-simplex polyhedral metrics converging to its Fubini–Study metric? The full question requires convergence to that metric and nonnegative Alexandrov curvature throughout. Mechanism: construct compatible polyhedral Kähler triangulations with mesh tending to zero and bound cone angles. The actual authored source explains Kähler rigidity and algebraic singular sets, citing Panov 2009 and de Borbon–Panov 2026. Decisive check: general PL approximation does not control codimension-two angle sums≤2π. **Defer:** cited proof bodies unread; no angle-controlled approximation, and no use of their recent theorem titles as evidence of a new solution.

5. **Zero-curvature geodesic avoidance.** P§15 pp9–10: on a genus-two surface with nonpositive curvature, does a random geodesic meet the negative-curvature region with probability one? Attribution is to Burago and a discussion with Burns, Brin and Pesin; a 2003 Rodriguez Hertz source and Wu 2015 are cited. Mechanism: show the invariant set trapped in the zero-curvature locus has Liouville measure zero, using recurrence plus a transverse expansion estimate. The source states Wu handles finitely many negative-curvature components. Decisive check: passing from finitely many to arbitrarily many components needs a uniform estimate; exhaustion alone does not preserve it. **Defer:** original proofs unread and no uniform estimate. This is an ergodic-geometric problem, not a random-point finite computation or a recycled stable/median family.

6. **Guth's small-volume sponge embedding.** P§18 p11: for every n is there ε_n>0 such that every bounded open subset of R^n of volume≤ε_n admits a length-increasing embedding into the unit ball? Guth's 2005 thesis is the attributed source; a 2016 Glynn-Adey thesis supplies a planar strip-target weakening. Mechanism: fold a thin cellular decomposition into a bounded target while preserving injectivity and a lower differential singular-value bound. Decisive check: volume alone does not bound diameter or topology; a strip construction supplies neither a ball target nor a uniform fold-separation estimate. **Reject for present depth:** no new mechanism beyond that missing estimate and original thesis bodies unread. Not ranked as a familiar hard filler.

7. **Maximal-distance minimizer reconstruction and uniqueness.** T§1.2 p2 Questions1.5–1.6 form ONE family: if Σ minimizes length among connected compact sets covering M within r, is it the unique r-minimizer for its own closed r-neighborhood B_r(Σ)? Does the energetic-point set G_Σ determine a minimizer for fixed M,r? Energetic means there is y∈M at distance r with the open ball B_r(y) disjoint from Σ. The source states Σ remains a minimizer for its neighborhood and distinguishes that elementary observation from uniqueness. Mechanism: prove equality rigidity in the covering constraint, or construct two inequivalent networks with exactly equal offset neighborhoods. Decisive check: equal lengths and common terminal points do not imply equal offset neighborhoods; a Steiner-tree tie alone is insufficient. **Provisional follow-up only:** actual original underlying [2] proof body unread, and no equal-neighborhood counterexample. Regularity Question1.4, horseshoe classification, random Steiner constants and every Steiner topology are NOT padded into more family counts.

8. **Compact realization of prescribed centers of distances.** G§7 p12 Problem34: given compact C⊂[0,∞) with 0∈C, is there compact K⊂R such that C(K)=C, where C(K)={a≥0:∀x∈K ∃y∈K, |x−y|=a}? Problem33's Borel variant belongs to the same inverse-realization family. The author dates the compact question to a 2020 workshop and cites Bartoszewicz et al., *On the operator of center of distances between the spaces of closed subsets of the real line*, DOI https://doi.org/10.12775/TMNA.2023.023 (2024), Theorem4.10 for a partial answer. Actual question body and nearby results read: arbitrary set realization by transfinite induction gives no descriptive/compactness control. Mechanism: intersect nested finite symmetric realizations while retaining a designated partner for every x and every a∈C. Decisive check: Hausdorff limits can add universal distances, so one also needs exclusion witnesses for every a outside C. **Provisional follow-up only:** cited original partial proof unread; no complete construction or safe exclusion invariant. Jones problems, Cantorval unions and spectrum questions are not counted as further new families.

## Ranking and history controls

Only the assigned Riesz persistence target retains a depth rank, with its nearest actual proof bodies read (ATTACK.md); it is unresolved and source scope is explicitly limited. No second or third source-cleared survivor is fabricated. Items7–8 have concrete next calculations but do not pass primary-proof/prior-art gates for ranking as actual survivors. This is a candid eight-family screen, not eight eligible nominations.

The historical screen uses canonical SUMMARY.md and discovery.md/discovery.json, not only SCOUTING. breadth-history.json contains31 matched canonical compact reports across both campaign paths, with full frozen files behind the capped display excerpts. There were generic lexical false hits for algebraic involutions and Fubini; they do not imply geometric duplicates. No exact compact report alias for the eight families was identified in this bounded screen. Absence from31 lexical hits does NOT exclude a paraphrase or an earlier source alias. The initial overinclusive path query reached historical copied reports; it was corrected to direct canonical lane files, with hash-deduplicated compact copies retained rather than hidden. No historical tree was copied recursively.

Active r231 arithmetic and r232 morphism/finite breadth remain excluded. No worker was polled or child started. The supplied assignment identifies their active subject areas; no completed report from them was assumed or invented. r230's eleven nonassigned families were excluded. All active/parked wavelet, multiplier, stable, median, quantile, BCC, projection and old MMPP directions remain excluded. No repeated inaccessible old source interval, forbidden access route, browser or registry mutation was used. Currentness is checked only for the main Riesz target; breadth novelty/current openness remains unverified.

# r233: unresolved, no outcome nomination

Read frozen actual 2410.22104v1 Theorem8/Remarks6–7 and UP24 2504.04845v1 Question5.1. Also retrieved/read the nearest 2409.16508v1 coefficient proof. ATTACK.md distinguishes the survey's undefined “equivalent distance” from the original zonal/two-point homogeneous setting and broader arbitrary-metric conjecture. No permission to change metrics was inferred. The exact intended invariance/equivalence meaning remains a source ambiguity; it is not silently resolved in favor of a counterexample.

Two routes: fixed projective-geodesic Jacobi sign persistence, with112 bounded parameter checks through64 modes and the actual Rodrigues sufficient-range bridge; and positive-kernel powers, with a complete generic matrix-power obstruction but no admissible metric counterexample. Neither settles the full source question. No PROOF.md, Lean, manuscript or acceptance claim. Eight distinct additional analysis/geometry families screened in SCOUTING.md; no novelty-cleared extra survivor ranked.

Guarded live arXiv metadata and author/object prior search retained; current public proof-registry head unavailable. An unrelated mathdb.org response is preserved as a failed registry identification. Original/copy SHA256 checks, primary PDF/text bindings and scientific failures retained. Manifest excludes itself and verification receipt; verifier runs separately after content writes. Only this assigned lane was written. Root alone accepts/counts:9 additional/39 total/next40 unchanged.

# Discovery disposition

NO COMPLETE CANDIDATE. Full Question5.1 remains unresolved. Fixed-sphere/chordal cases and integer exponent multiples are known/source consequences and uncredited. The matrix entrywise-power obstruction is an explanatory helper, not an answer. Finite coefficient scans and degree-one positivity do not settle all modes or all exponents. Eight breadth screens have no certified novel survivor. No counterexample based on an altered or nonhomogeneous metric is nominated. Metric scope ambiguity, unavailable current registry head and unread older breadth proof bodies block eligibility clearance.

See ATTACK.md for full scientific reasoning; SCOUTING.md for new-family screening; provenance.jsonl, retrieval.jsonl and text-bindings.json for immutable source evidence; jacobi-checks.json and checks.py for reproducible bounded numerics.
